section: Educational Psychology · Ch11-12 — Personality & Individual Differences
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: The 'Big Five' model describing personality along dimensions such as Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism belongs to which broad approach?
explanation: Trait theories (Big Five/OCEAN, also Cattell's 16PF) describe personality as measurable dimensions present in varying degrees in everyone. Type theories sort people into discrete categories (e.g. Sheldon's body types); psychoanalytic theory (Freud) emphasises unconscious conflict.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11-12 — Personality & Individual Differences
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: In Freud's structural model, the part of personality that operates on the 'pleasure principle', seeking immediate gratification without regard for consequences, is the:
explanation: The id is the primitive, instinct-driven part working on the pleasure principle. The ego operates on the reality principle, mediating between id, superego and external reality; the superego represents internalised moral standards.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11-12 — Personality & Individual Differences
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A pupil who can generate many different, unusual uses for a simple brick (e.g. paperweight, doorstop, art material) is displaying strong:
explanation: Divergent thinking generates multiple original solutions/uses — the hallmark of creativity (J.P. Guilford). Convergent thinking narrows toward one correct answer, as in typical exam-style problems.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11-12 — Personality & Individual Differences
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Two children of the same age in the same class differ widely in reading ability, interests and social confidence. The main factors responsible for such individual differences are:

options.option_text: Interaction of heredity and environment (home, culture, experiences)
Heredity alone, since environment plays no measurable role
Random chance with no identifiable causes

explanation: Individual differences arise from the continuous interaction of hereditary endowment and diverse environmental/experiential factors — the same nature-nurture interaction underlying broader development.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch11-12 — Personality & Individual Differences
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teacher seats a child with mild hearing loss in the front row, uses visual cues alongside speech, and pairs them with a peer buddy — while keeping the child in the same regular classroom as everyone else. This approach reflects:

options.option_text: Integration only, with no curriculum accommodation

explanation: Inclusive education keeps children with disabilities in the mainstream classroom with reasonable accommodations tailored to need — distinct from segregation (separate special schools) or mere physical integration without support.
